decision: Compare accounting policies by agent utility at independently expert-set budgets, using a common post-hoc V3 exposure risk scale.

arms.enforcement: release, influence, and outcome fact ceilings at the shared root task
successful query-response count ceiling, including zero-row and negative answers; V3 facts computed audit-only
cumulative visible-row ceiling; V3 facts computed audit-only
cumulative response bytes buffered before release; V3 facts computed audit-only

sampling.assignment: within-task paired arms; arm order uses a balanced Latin square; each run receives a fresh database and root-task snapshot

budget_calibration.independence: calibration and approval use disjoint non-author panels with three practitioners per domain; neither sees ground truth, agent traces, or outcomes
budget_calibration.training: unit cards plus two training tasks excluded from analysis
budget_calibration.aggregation: per-task, per-arm median of independent calibration ceilings, then frozen for the disjoint approval panel

approval_adjudication.rule: per task/arm, majority reject prevents execution; ties reject conservatively
approval_adjudication.approved_ceiling: otherwise freeze the component-wise median of non-reject approved or narrowed ceilings, capped by the requested ceiling
approval_adjudication.rejected_observation: record every registered seed as approval_rejected with zero completion

blind_grading.panel: six additional non-author practitioners, two per domain, disjoint from calibration and approval
blind_grading.coverage: every completed run receives two independent grades for every blind-expert and trace-guardrail rubric item
blind_grading.aggregation: arithmetic mean by run and rubric item

primary_metrics.definition: sum of predeclared weighted automated, blind-expert, and trace-guardrail item scores
primary_metrics.decision_use: answer quality under the approved policy budget

primary_metrics.definition: rubric score at least 80 and every task-specific critical item score at least 0.8
primary_metrics.decision_use: whether the workflow achieved the business decision rather than merely returning data

human_usability_metrics.definition: monotonic time from fully rendered request to approve, reject, or narrow
rejected requests divided by all independently reviewed requests
approved requests whose ceilings or scopes were reduced divided by approved requests

common_risk_metrics.definition: post-hoc union of V3 release, influence, and outcome facts, weighted by the catalog sensitivity card fixed before study collection
blind trace-review count of fields outside the task's declared decision need

analysis.unit: task-agent-seed run, paired by task and seed across arms
analysis.binary_inference: within-task-and-seed paired differences in critical-goal completion
analysis.approval_inference: per-review decision time, rejection, and conditional-on-approval narrowing, clustered by task
analysis.uncertainty: task-cluster bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and exact task-level sign-flip tests
analysis.multiple_comparisons: Holm correction for the three TaskGate-versus-baseline rubric-score contrasts
analysis.missing_runs: report and retain failures as zero completion; never silently drop budget exhaustion or tool errors

guardrails: No paper claim may call this a workflow study while status is designed_not_collected.
Templates and synthetic records are not expert judgments or agent outcomes.
The same frozen model, prompt, tool surface, database snapshot, and seed schedule are used across arms.
Baseline arms are compared on post-hoc V3 risk, not on incomparable native budget units.
Human graders are blind to arm, budget, model trace identifiers, and paper hypothesis.
